import { GeneralistReleaseTimeline } from '@/components/interactive/generalist-release-timeline';

A generalist robot policy is one learned model trained to perform many tasks, often on several robot bodies <Cite id="tri-lbm-2025" />.

<Image id="gemini-robotics-apollo-franka-2025" />

Outside the [VLA line](/manipulation/vla-models/) and [Physical Intelligence's π models](/manipulation/pi-line/), the main 2026 lines are Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2-2026" />, NVIDIA's GR00T, Figure's Helix, AgiBot's GO series, Skild AI and Generalist AI. Toggle "Downloadable only" to filter the timeline's 13 selected records, an authored selection.

<GeneralistReleaseTimeline className="my-6" />

## Gemini Robotics

DeepMind's March 2025 report introduces a Gemini 2.0-based family: Gemini Robotics-ER for spatial and temporal understanding, and Gemini Robotics, which builds on ER to produce robot actions <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2025" />. The launch post says Gemini Robotics more than doubles performance on a comprehensive generalization benchmark against other state-of-the-art VLAs <Cite id="gemini-robotics-blog-2025" />.

<Image id="gemini-robotics-aloha-dexterous-2025" />

The 1.5 report, first submitted to arXiv on October 2, 2025, interleaves natural-language thinking with VLA actions, introduces Motion Transfer across embodiments and uses the separate GR-ER 1.5 model as an orchestrator <Cite id="gemini-robotics-15-2025" />. The launch post, dated September 25, 2025, made ER 1.5 available through the Gemini API and Gemini Robotics 1.5 to select partners <Cite id="gemini-robotics-15-blog-2025" />, after On-Device (June 2025) became the first DeepMind VLA offered for fine-tuning, to trusted testers <Cite id="gemini-robotics-on-device-2025" />.

On July 30, 2026, DeepMind announced Gemini Robotics 2 as three models: a VLA, the embodied-reasoning VLM ER 2, and On-Device 2 for local operation. Apollo 2 walks, crouches and stretches to manipulate objects, and one checkpoint runs Apollo 2 with 22-<Term id="degrees-of-freedom">DoF</Term> SharpaWave hands or Inspire hands and Franka Duo with the Robotiq gripper; DeepMind says On-Device 2 adapts to new bi-arm embodiments in a few hours, typically with fewer than 200 examples <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2-2026" />. The ER 2 post adds success detection on raw video feeds <Cite id="gemini-robotics-er-2-2026" />.

DeepMind's image alt text reports whole-body averages on Apollo with Inspire hands of 76.3% for picking from a shelf, 68.4% from a table and 45.7% from the floor. Single-task results on Apollo with Sharpa hands are 92% for unscrewing a bulb, 36% for screwing one in, 44% for tying a trash bag, 40% for Ziplock and 32% for Dustpan. Trial counts and error bars are unexplained, and DeepMind concludes that "the multi-finger dexterous manipulation remains challenging" <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2-2026" />.

The 1.5 model card specifies continuous numerical actions but no action-head family, chunk lengths, command rate or parameter count <Cite id="gemini-robotics-15-2025" />. The Gemini Robotics 2 announcement also omits them, the VLA went only to early-access partners, and weight and licence terms are undisclosed <Cite id="gemini-robotics-2-2026" />. DeepMind validates its Veo-based [world-model](/world-models/) policy simulator against more than 1,600 real trials of eight Gemini Robotics checkpoints <Cite id="veo-world-simulator-2025" />.

## GR00T: the open humanoid line

GR00T N1 (March 2025) couples a <Term id="vision-language-model">VLM</Term> backbone to a <Term id="flow-matching">flow-matching</Term> diffusion-transformer action head and links the public GR00T-N1-2B checkpoint <Cite id="gr00t-n1-2025" />. N1.5 freezes the VLM in pretraining and fine-tuning <Cite id="gr00t-n1-5-2025" />, and N1.6, which doubles the DiT to 32 layers, outperforms N1.5 in simulation and on real YAM, AgiBot Genie-1 and Unitree G1 robots, NVIDIA reports <Cite id="gr00t-n1-6-2025" />.

The Isaac-GR00T repository lists N1.7 on April 18, 2026, with a Cosmos-Reason2-2B backbone, a 3B-parameter base checkpoint and relative end-effector actions shared by robot and human embodiments; pretraining adds 20K hours of EgoScale human video <Cite id="isaac-gr00t-repo-2026" />, which the EgoScale paper puts at over 20,854 hours <Cite id="egoscale-2026" />. The README's licence section assigns Apache 2.0 to code and the NVIDIA Open Model License to weights, while its introduction calls N1.7 "fully commercially licensable under Apache 2.0" <Cite id="isaac-gr00t-repo-2026" />.

## Figure Helix

Figure's February 20, 2025 Helix post pairs S2, an internet-pretrained VLM producing a latent task representation at 7 to 9 Hz, with S1, a visuomotor transformer that reads it with images and robot state at 200 Hz and outputs wrist, finger, torso and head targets <Cite id="helix-2025" />.

Figure's January 27, 2026 Helix 02 post adds S0, a 10M-parameter whole-body controller that outputs joint-level actuator commands at 1 kHz beneath S1's 200 Hz full-body joint targets. Figure says S0 trains entirely in simulation on over 1,000 hours of retargeted human motion and replaces 109,504 lines of hand-written C++, and describes its dishwasher demonstration as one continuous four-minute task with 61 loco-manipulation actions, no resets and no human intervention <Cite id="helix-02-2026" />. Neither Helix post gives repeated-trial success tables or release terms for the trained policies <Cite id="helix-2025" /> <Cite id="helix-02-2026" />.

Figure's August 25, 2026 Index announcement counts over 16M uploaded videos and commits over \$1B over 12 months to data and compute <Cite id="figure-index-2026" />, and Figure reports that Index pretraining, all else fixed, lifted Helix 2.5's zero-shot success in 30 unseen homes from 9% to 56% <Cite id="helix-2-5-2026" />.

## AgiBot: GO-1 and GO-2

The AgiBot World report (March 2025) introduces GO-1, whose latent action model learns from consecutive video frames, so training can include unlabeled human video alongside cross-embodiment robot data <Cite id="agibot-world-2025" />. AgiBot presents GO-2 as closing a "Semantic-Actuation Gap": a lower-frequency System 2 generates structured action sequences, a higher-frequency System 1 combines them with live observations, and teacher forcing trains the executor to follow imperfect reasoning. The announcement gives only relative rates for the two modules and says the work was accepted at CVPR 2026 and ACL 2026 <Cite id="agibot-go2-2026" />.

AgiBot reports 98.5% average success across the four LIBERO suites, 86.6% zero-shot in LIBERO-Plus environments with disturbances, and 82.9% real-world success for a model trained only on simulation. It claims superiority over π0.5 and GR00T without trial counts, uncertainty, disturbance protocol or comparator versions <Cite id="agibot-go2-2026" />, and on LIBERO-Plus typical VLAs drop from 95% to below 30% under modest perturbations <Cite id="libero-plus-2025" />.

## Skild AI

Skild AI's January 14, 2026 [Series C](/market-map/) raised \$1.4 billion at a valuation of over \$14 billion. Skild calls its model "omni-bodied", names simulation and Internet video for pretraining and teleoperation and deployments for post-training, and says the model can control robots without prior knowledge of their body form. Architecture, parameter count, control rate, chunk horizon, benchmark protocol and weight terms are not given <Cite id="skild-series-c-2026" />.

A September 2025 post describes training on 100,000 simulated robots <Cite id="skild-omni-bodied-2025" />. Skild presents S1 (August 18, 2026) as an in-context learner: shown a video of a task, it executes it, and on unseen long-horizon tasks of 4 to 8 minutes Skild reports 66% cumulative per-step success, against 9% for language prompting <Cite id="skild-s1-2026" />. The company also reports passing \$100M in annual recurring revenue <Cite id="skild-arr-2026" />.

## Generalist AI

Generalist AI says GEN-0 (November 2025) is pretrained on over 270,000 hours of [real-world manipulation data](/data-hardware/data-bottleneck/), growing by 10,000 hours a week <Cite id="generalist-gen0-2025" />. It reports that GEN-1 (April 2026), trained from scratch on half a million hours, reaches 99% average success on tasks where earlier models achieve 64%, with 1 hour of robot data per task <Cite id="generalist-gen1-2026" />, and that GEN-1.5 (August 2026) learns a task in context from one 3 to 12 second demonstration, with 59% average one-shot success across 10 tasks <Cite id="gen-1-5-2026" />.

## Independent evaluation

RoboArena ranks generalist policies through double-blind pairwise trials at seven institutions, with more than 600 real-robot episodes across seven policies <Cite id="roboarena-2025" />, and TRI evaluates its Large Behavior Models in blind, randomized trials with statistical confidence <Cite id="tri-lbm-2025" />.

<Image id="roboarena-evaluation-2025" />

## Human-video transfer

Physical Intelligence and Georgia Tech co-fine-tune π0.5 on human data, with 3D hand positions as actions, and relevant robot data, and transfer improves with the quantity and diversity of robot pretraining <Cite id="pi-human-to-robot-2025" />. EgoScale adds aligned human-robot mid-training and finds scale and alignment complementary <Cite id="egoscale-2026" />. [Cross-embodiment transfer](/manipulation/cross-embodiment/) compares them.

Steertuning, from Lerrel Pinto and colleagues at NYU (October 2026), pretrains a 400M-parameter diffusion policy on egocentric human video alone, then adapts it to a new task from 5 human demonstrations with 2 minutes of LoRA fine-tuning and steering toward the closest demonstration. On a mobile manipulator the authors report 71% average success over 12 new tasks, 9 in a rented home and 3 in their lab. On the lab tasks it succeeded in 25 of 30 trials, against 7 with steering alone and none with the short fine-tune alone <Cite id="steertuning-2026" />.

--- title: "The Pi Line" description: "pi0 to pi0.7: flow-matching action experts, FAST tokenization, open-world generalization, and source-scoped checkpoint availability." domain: manipulation slug: pi-line order: 5 status: published lastReviewed: "2026-08-17" citations: - pi0-2024 - pi0-fast-2025 - pi05-2025 - knowledge-insulation-paper-2025 - knowledge-insulation-2025 - pi06-model-card-2025 - pistar06-2025 - pistar06-blog-2025 - mem-2026 - pi07-2026 - pi07-blog-2026 - openpi-repo-2024 - real-time-chunking-2025 - pi0-blog-2024 - paligemma-2024 - lipman-flow-matching-2022 - openpi-blog-2025 - pi-real-time-chunking-blog-2025 - rectified-flow-2022 - jetson-ai-lab-openpi-thor - pi-fast-blog-2025 - hi-robot-blog-2025 - garg-self-demonstrated-control-2026 - gemma3-2025 - pi-olympics-2025 - pi-partner-2026 - cfgrl-2025 - pi-rl-2026 - mem-blog-2026 - rlt-2026 - training-time-rtc-2025 - bagel-2025 - pi-human-to-robot-2025 - droid-2024 - libero-2023 - gemini-robotics-2025 - openvla-oft-2025 seeAlso: - "manipulation/rl-finetuning" - "manipulation/cross-embodiment" - "frontier/generalization" --- import { FlowMatchingTrajectory } from '@/components/interactive/flow-matching-trajectory'; import { PiGenerationTimeline } from '@/components/interactive/pi-generation-timeline'; The pi line is Physical Intelligence's series of [vision-language-action models](/manipulation/vla-models/), from π0 (October 2024) to π0.7 (April 2026) . π0 kept a pretrained vision-language backbone and replaced discrete action tokens with a flow-matching action expert . Later models changed tokenization, training data, memory and prompting. Drag the integration steps slider from 1 upward to watch the cloud reach the action modes. ## π0: the action expert π0 grafts a second transformer, the action expert of about 300M parameters, onto a pretrained vision-language model initialized from PaliGemma; the backbone handles image and text tokens, and the expert's 50 action tokens attend into it at every layer through shared self-attention. Inputs are 2 or 3 RGB images, language and proprioceptive state, and the model predicts H = 50 actions, executing 16 per inference at 20 Hz on UR5e and Franka or 25 at 50 Hz on the other robots . PaliGemma itself couples a SigLIP vision encoder to a Gemma language model for transfer across vision-language tasks . Where [Diffusion Policy](/manipulation/diffusion-policy/) denoises with a DDPM, π0 trains the expert with conditional flow matching on a straight path. Training samples noise $\varepsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I)$, forms $A_t^\tau = \tau A_t + (1 - \tau)\varepsilon$, and regresses $v_\theta$ onto $u = A_t - \varepsilon$. Inference integrates from $\tau = 0$ to $\tau = 1$ in 10 forward-Euler steps, with the image-text-state prefix KV-cached once so each step recomputes only the action suffix . Lipman et al. found optimal-transport paths more efficient than diffusion paths for training and sampling .
Cross-embodiment pre-training combines single-arm, dual-arm and mobile manipulators across 7 robot configurations. The base model reaches what the authors call "rudimentary proficiency", and complex tasks such as laundry folding use curated post-training data . PI says π0, π0-FAST and π0.5 executed chunks synchronously, waiting for inference after each one , which the RTC paper later compared with asynchronous execution on π0.5 . ## Why ten steps is enough A DDPM path curves through noise space, while rectified flow straightens paths so that coarse time steps simulate them accurately . Each Euler step costs a forward pass through the expert: π0 uses 10 steps , π0.6 uses five , and π0.7 also uses five . Consistency and one-step distillation, covered in [Diffusion Policy](/manipulation/diffusion-policy/), pursue the same saving. ## π0-FAST: compressed action tokens FAST traces the failure of per-dimension, per-timestep binning to highly correlated tokens, which make next-token prediction trivial; policies with this naive tokenization make no progress on table bussing at 20 Hz or T-shirt folding at 50 Hz . FAST instead applies a discrete cosine transform along time, rounds the coefficients and byte-pair-encodes the result, and its universal FAST+ tokenizer is trained on about one million one-second action chunks across embodiments , or "1M real robot action sequences" in PI's post . Trained on a 10k-hour cross-embodied mixture, π0-FAST matches π0's generalist performance with up to five times fewer GPU hours. Inference costs more: about 750 ms per one-second chunk on an NVIDIA 4090, against within 100 ms for diffusion π0, since decoding needs 30 to 60 tokens instead of ten steps . The Knowledge Insulation note reports that π0-FAST took twice as long to finish single-embodiment table bussing . ## π0.5 and Knowledge Insulation π0.5 targets open-world generalization . It keeps the π0 skeleton, adds training examples that interleave images, language commands, object detections, subtask predictions and low-level actions, and at inference first predicts a language subtask ("pick up the plate"), then conditions the action expert on it. In long-horizon mobile manipulation in new homes, removing either cross-embodiment data source significantly hurts home-task scores, while removing web data leaves those scores nearly unchanged but strongly hurts language following and subtask inference . The Knowledge Insulation paper turns the two-stage π0.5 approach into one stage: the expert trains with flow matching for continuous inference, and the backbone trains on discrete FAST tokens, vision-language data and planning data, with expert gradients stopped at the backbone keys and values . With a frozen backbone, shirt folding drops to 0%; on generalist table bussing, π0 needs 7.5 times as many training steps to match; and vision-language co-training also gives the joint-training baseline good language following without stop-gradient . The openpi π0.5 checkpoints were trained with KI, but the repository supports only the flow-matching head , so outside groups reimplement the FAST loss and KI . ## π0.6 and π*0.6: scaling and experience The π0.6 model card, dated November 17, 2025, initializes the backbone from Gemma3 4B, gives the action expert about 860M parameters and keeps expert gradients out of the backbone. Without task-specific fine-tuning, π0.6 folds laundry reliably and fully assembles the box 20% of the time, tasks that previously needed fine-tuning to succeed at all . In PI's Robot Olympics, fine-tuned π0.6 averaged 52% success and 72% task progress, while a fine-tuned standard VLM without π0.6's robot pre-training had no successes and 9% progress . π*0.6 uses Recap to learn from demonstrations, expert teleoperation corrections and autonomous experience, with a language-conditioned value function whose advantage, against a task-dependent threshold, gives each action a binary improvement indicator; human corrections are forced positive, and evaluation samples with the positive indicator . The report places this formulation closest to CFGRL , while outside groups find RL on flow-based π0 and π0.5 hard because flow matching makes action log-likelihoods intractable . The companion blog's example is a bad portafilter grasp that causes a later insertion failure . On a rig with two 6-DoF arms and 50 Hz joint-position control, on-robot experience more than doubles successful completions per hour for double-shot espresso and diverse laundry, tested on a button-up shirt, against offline RL plus demonstration fine-tuning. Failures fall by "about a factor of two" ("more than 2×" in the figure), the "90%+" summary excludes diverse laundry, and the box task reports stages separately, with remaining failures mostly in final placement . PI published MEM on March 3, 2026 . π0.6-MEM pairs a video encoder with a high-level policy that predicts updated natural-language summaries of earlier events, and handles tasks needing up to fifteen minutes of memory, such as recipe setup and kitchen cleanup. Its adaptation experiments train memory and memoryless policies on the same corrections, such as which way to open a refrigerator . ## RL tokens On March 19, 2026, PI described RL tokens: small actor and critic networks train online on a compressed, frozen token from π0.6, speeding up the most precise stages of four tasks by up to 3×; Ethernet insertion took two hours of training with 15 minutes of robot data . [RL fine-tuning](/manipulation/rl-finetuning/) covers the wider method family. ## π0.7: generalization as a prompting problem π0.7 treats underspecified prompts as the [generalization](/frontier/generalization/) bottleneck. It is π0.6 plus MEM at about 5B parameters, and training simulates real-time chunking delays of 0 to 12 timesteps, up to 240 ms on a 50 Hz robot , the training-time RTC method that on π0.6 matched inference-time RTC at lower compute . The context holds task and subtask language, with the subtask from a learned high-level policy or a human, and episode metadata on quality, speed and mistakes; training uses different subsets of this context but always keeps the joint or end-effector control-mode label. Multi-view subgoal images come from a BAGEL-initialized world model, and subgoal and subtask generation run in separate threads . BAGEL is a unified decoder-only model pretrained on trillions of interleaved tokens . π0.7 folds laundry on a bimanual UR5e with no laundry data for that robot, matching the task progress of experienced teleoperators trying it there for the first time . In the air-fryer example, language coaching fine-tunes a high-level policy that generates the subtasks without new teleoperation, which the authors call "early signs of compositional task generalization" . [Human video](/manipulation/cross-embodiment/) joins the line through π0.5 co-fine-tuning, which roughly doubles performance on scenarios seen only in human data . ## Which checkpoints are listed PI released π0's code and weights in openpi on February 4, 2025, saying 1 to 20 hours of data sufficed to fine-tune a variety of tasks . The openpi README at the pinned commit of August 24, 2026 lists base checkpoints for π0, π0-FAST and π0.5, plus π0-FAST, π0 and π0.5 models fine-tuned on DROID and a π0.5 LIBERO model . DROID holds 76k trajectories from 564 scenes , and LIBERO has 130 tasks in four suites . In two outside comparisons, Google DeepMind's re-implementation trained on its own mixture beat the public π0 checkpoint , and OpenVLA with the OFT recipe outperformed π0 fine-tuned with its default recipe .
